Commentary.Commentary: We are back for Sri Lanka's reply! The umpires are back out in the middle followed by the English players. Nishan Madushka and Dimuth Karunaratne will be opening for Sri Lanka. Chris Woakes gets the job to start with the new ball. Here we go...
... FOURTH INNINGS ...

Sri Lanka, on the other hand, bowled a lot better and their pacers were much more disciplined. The fielding and catching was on point as well, but the problem for them was they conceded a big first innings lead. Asitha Fernando and Lahiru Kumara were the pick of the bowlers with three wickets each while Milan Rathnayake got a couple. The lone spinner, Prabath Jayasuriya chipped in with two as well, but just like in the first innings, they had no answers to the batting masterclass of Joe Root. Now, their batters have an extremely tough ask to chase down this huge total, but the pitch has not deteriorated that much, and they have plenty of time as well. They need to take inspiration from their second innings from the last Test and go in with a positive intent. Join us in a bit for the start of the exciting run chase in the final session!

England set up a mammoth target of 483 runs! With that, the umpires have taken early Tea on Day 3. Undoubtedly, the hosts have a clear advantage and also have around 2 and a half days to bowl the visitors out to take an unassailable lead in the series. Once again, it was a master class from arguably the best batter the country has ever produced. Yes, we are talking about Joe Root who broke records for fun in this innings. Firstly, he surpassed Graham Gooch for the most number of Test runs at Lord's, and then he broke Alastair Cook's record of most centuries by an English batter in this format. Before this game, he did not have two centuries in one Test, and he completed that as well. Root will go down as one of the best batters in history and this game just shows a glimpse of his legacy.

OUT! TAKEN! Another Joe Root masterclass comes to an end! Top knock. This is banged in short and on middle. Root pulls but not a lot of distance on it. Kamindu Mendis at deep square leg, runs to his right and takes it. Root walks off the field to a huge round of applause from everyone present in the crowd whether it being a rival fan or a Sri Lankan player. England have been bowled out for 251!

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the post-Lunch session on Day 3! The umpires are out in the middle and so are the players of Sri Lanka. Joe Root is all set to resume his stay on the crease alongside Jamie Smith. Milan Rathnayake be bowling the first over after the Lunch break. Let's play...
... DAY 3, SESSION 2 ...

Sri Lanka were good with the new ball and they also got the rewards but as the ball got old, they just conceded a lot of runs. For now, they can just be patient by hitting the right lines and lengths. Probably stem the run flow a touch and try and pick wickets. Can they show some fight after the break? Join us at 12.40 pm GMT.

Session Summary - 134 runs, 27 overs, and 3wickets! England continues to pile the misery on the Lankans! Their lead is now close to 400 and we feel, they’ll continue to bat for longer. They lost a couple early but Brook and Root put up a good stand and they scored at a decent rate. Brook fell but Smith has continued the good work with Root who seems in fine touch. More of the same is what England will be hoping for.
Gives this one some more air, full and on off, Jamie Smith uses his feet and drills it wide of long on for a brace. THAT WILL BE LUNCH ON DAY 3!

Commentary.Commentary: In all readiness for the action on Day 3 to begin! The two umpires stride out to the middle, followed by the Lankans as they take their positions. Ben Duckett and Ollie Pope are on their way to the crease to resume their innings for England. Lahiru Kumara will get the job to start the proceeding for Sri Lanka. Also, we have spotted that Dinesh Chandimal is wearing the keeping glove and he will be standing behind the sticks for Sri Lanka in place of Nishan Madushka. Let's play...

Sri Lanka will be disappointed with both their bowling and batting performances. After winning the toss and opting to bowl, their bowlers started strong but became expensive as the innings progressed, putting pressure on the batters to compensate. Unfortunately, the batting lineup collapsed under the weight of this pressure, with only Kamindu Mendis putting up a fight, adding crucial runs before falling while trying to accelerate the innings. As they head into 'Moving Day,' Sri Lanka's focus will be on taking early wickets and putting England under pressure. By the end of the day, we should have a clearer idea of where this Test is heading. Stay tuned for what promises to be another gripping day of Test cricket.

The game has moved quickly, bringing us to the third inning with England holding a strong 256-run lead. Day 2 was dominated by the home team, with Gus Atkinson and Matthew Potts leading the charge to post 427 runs, aided by the tail-enders. England's bowlers then bowled Sri Lanka out for under 200, maintaining their grip on the game. In their second innings, England lost Dan Lawrence in the final overs of the day, though only after a successful review from Sri Lanka. With a solid lead, England will aim to keep up the momentum and push hard to secure their second win in this three-match Test series.

Hello and a warm welcome to Day 3 of this thrilling second Test match between England and Sri Lanka at Lord's Cricket Ground in London. As we head into what is often referred to as 'Moving Day', the stage is set for another exciting chapter in this encounter. England currently holds a commanding position, but there's still plenty of time for the visitors to stage a comeback.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, that is it from an entertaining Day 2. England have a healthy lead going into the 'Moving Day' and looks set to post a massive target. Sri Lanka needs some kind of a miracle to save this Test. Day 3 will begin on 31st August, Saturday at 10 am GMT, but you can join us early for all the build-up. Cheers!

In the final session, Sri Lanka faced an uphill battle with just three wickets remaining and a significant gap to bridge to avoid the follow-on. Jayasuriya provided solid support to Mendis but made the costly decision to attack the spinner, resulting in his dismissal. Mendis, however, remained unfazed, continuing to score quickly. England turned to their spinners, but Mendis held firm, reaching his half-century. A brilliant piece of fielding from Ollie Pope resulted in Lahiru Kumara's run-out, opening the door for England to wrap up the innings. Mendis was eventually dismissed for 74, with Sri Lanka conceding a hefty 231-run lead. England opted not to enforce the follow-on and came out to bat, losing Dan Lawrence early but managing to add over 20 runs, extending their lead to more than 250 runs.

The second session was dominated entirely by England. Their pacers maintained disciplined line and length, with Woakes in particularly fiery form. They prevented Sri Lanka from forming any partnerships, consistently taking wickets at regular intervals. Ollie Pope's strategic field placements and timely bowling changes paid off perfectly. England managed to take five wickets in the session, with Potts and Stone each taking two wickets in the same over. However, Kamindu Mendis emerged as a resilient figure for Sri Lanka. Known for his reliability in the lower order, Mendis began a fightback as the teams headed into the final session.

England entered Day 2 in a strong position and only strengthened their grip on the match. Gus Atkinson picked up right where he left off, playing some elegant shots. The crowd and his teammates were more nervous than he was as he approached the 90s, but he confidently struck two beautiful boundaries to reach his maiden Test century. Matthew Potts provided solid support before being dismissed, with the pair taking England’s total past the 400-run mark. Olly Stone added some valuable runs lower down the order. Asitha Fernando was the standout bowler, claiming the remaining three wickets to complete a well-deserved five-wicket haul. Sri Lanka, facing a large total, suffered an early setback when Madushka was dismissed quickly. Karunaratne and Nissanka attempted to stabilize the innings, but Karunaratne’s dismissal in the final over before lunch left Sri Lanka on the back foot.

England continue their dominance on Day 2! It began with a brilliant century from Gus Atkinson, and the bowlers followed suit by restricting Sri Lanka and securing a lead of over 200 runs. Sri Lanka now faces a daunting challenge if they want to preserve their decade-long unbeaten Test record against England at Lord's.
